_description:
# The user zone: how to ask the user

The user (the human) is also something that can receive letters. Their zone is `~/.aos/user/` (one per Linux account and machine; it is the user's own stack). Its `mailbox/` is an ordinary aos mailbox. Send a letter there when only the user can do it; the answer comes back to your own mailbox as a normal letter (with `in_reply_to`), and `mail_notify` wakes you as usual.

- who should send, and what: `aos/user_zone.json#/what`
- how to send (with a shell, or with aos tools only): `aos/user_zone.json#/send`
- what the answer looks like, and how far you may trust it: `aos/user_zone.json#/answer`
- the door (the notice on the zone, read it before sending): `~/.aos/user/door.json`; the user's card: `~/aos-home/ws/public/user.json`
what:
# What to send to the user

Every letter has a `kind`:

- `decide`: a question only the user can decide. Every question has options (`key` 1-8 letters/digits, `label`, optional `consequence`), a `recommend` that is one of the keys, and `eli5` (two plain sentences). At most 7 questions in one letter.
  One question: `{"id": "q1", "question": "one line", "eli5": "two plain sentences", "options": [{"key": "a", "label": "do it", "consequence": "two more days"}, {"key": "b", "label": "skip"}], "recommend": "a", "why": "optional", "details": "optional", "source_path": "optional"}`.
- `verify`: please try it on the real machine. Say what to do (`what`) and when it counts as done (`done_when`).
- `trial`: please play with it and tell me how it feels.
- `chore`: something only the user can do (log in, plug in). Needs `done_when`.
- `fyi`: just so you know. The user puts it away; usually no answer comes.

Do not send: progress (use the board), requests between agents, questions you can find out yourself.

Optional keys: `urgent` (true only when no answer blocks everything), `deadline` (`2026-11-15` = by the end of that day, or a local time `2026-11-15T18:00`), `default_if_silent` (what you will do if no answer by the deadline; needs `deadline`; not allowed with `risk: irreversible`; the user may undo it later), `risk` (`normal` or `irreversible` for push, delete, sending outside), `dedupe_key` (same question from two agents is shown once, and both get the answer), `origin` (who first asked, when you pass a question on; paste it unchanged).
send:
# How to send

With a shell (claude, codex bodies):

```sh
~/aos-home/ws/tools/aos-user/aos-user send --kind decide --title "one line that makes sense alone" < letter.json
```

`letter.json` holds `what` (one or two sentences: what you need; optional for decide) and the keys from `#/what` (for decide: `questions`). The tool fills `zone`, `from` (your stack name), `to`, `status`, `host`, and the reply address (`$AOS_STACK/mailbox`, or `--reply-to MAILBOX`). It checks the letter against `~/.aos/user/schema/letter.json` first; a bad letter is not sent (`SchemaBad`, with the reason). It prints the letter name.

With aos tools only (agent-fsm bodies): tool `user_send` if you have it (ask for it to be added if not), as you: `{"kind": "decide", "title": "...", "questions": [...]}` (the same keys as above, checked the same way; the answer comes to your mailbox). Without `user_send` the old way still works. `mailbox_send` `{"box": "/home/<you>/.aos/user/mailbox", "status": "NEEDS-USER", "title": "...", "what": "...", "decide": "the question, the options, your recommendation"}`. The user sees it marked as old format and answers in words.

The zone checks every new letter within a minute. A letter that breaks the door's rules, or more than 10 letters from you within one hour, is moved to the zone's `rejected/` and comes back to your mailbox: status `FAILED`, title `Returned: ...`, `in_reply_to` = your letter, `reason` = what was wrong. The user does not see it. Fix the letter and send it again; do not send it again unchanged, and group questions into one letter (at most 7) instead of sending many.

Never read the zone with `aos-mailbox read` or `mailbox_read`: they delete letters. Never write anything in the zone except by sending a letter to its `mailbox/`. An eca body may have the hook `user_zone_guard` (`lib/agent/user_zone_guard` under `$AOS_HOME`, event `before_tool`): it blocks an aos tool call that would touch the zone outside `mailbox/`.
answer:
# The answer

The user answers with `aos-user answer` / `reply` / `ok` or on the zone web page (127.0.0.1 only). A letter stays waiting until it is answered ("answered = gone").

The answer is a letter in your mailbox with `in_reply_to` = your letter's name, status `DONE`, the usual fields (`from` = `user`, `title` = `Re: ...`, `what` = the answer in words), and also: `answers` (`[{id, answer, differs}]`; `differs` = not the recommended one; `answer` may be `other` = see `note`), `answer_line` (the same in decide-page form, `q1:a、q2:c*（備註：...）`), `note`, `text`, `via` (`cli` or `web`), `answered_at`, `host`, `letter_hash`, `reply_id`, `auth`.

Check it: `~/aos-home/ws/tools/aos-user/aos-user verify <the answer's letter folder>` compares it with the zone's own copy (`done/`) and log. `ok:` = it was sent from the zone.

How far to trust it (the user decided this on 11-13): a checked answer from the zone counts as the user's own words, also for push and delete (AGENTS.md rule 2). But all agents run as the same Linux user: an agent with a shell could fake the zone's copy and log too. The check stops passing-on ("the user told me yes") and fake letters dropped into your mailbox; it does not stop an agent that sets out to forge both sides. Do not try to.
